title: Jalpaiguri's Amarpur tea estate suspends work after protests over unpaid Puja bonus
dek: About 300 workers found the gate locked on Thursday morning, after weeks of protests over the 6.2% of their 20% bonus that was still unpaid.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Workers at the Amarpur Tea Estate in Jalpaiguri district found the garden's main gate locked on Thursday morning, with a notice at the entrance announcing a "suspension of work", one report said. About 300 workers and their families are affected.

The closure follows several days of protests over the annual Durga Puja bonus. Workers had demanded the full 20% bonus, but the management paid 13.8% before the Puja and promised to clear the remaining 6.2% before Diwali, according to the report. When the balance was not paid on time, workers continued their protest. The management has not made a public statement on the closure.

Workers said they would approach the state Labour Department, the district magistrate and the chief minister to seek the garden's immediate reopening.

Suspensions of work over bonus disputes are a recurring problem in the Dooars and Terai tea belt, where gardens have shut in past seasons after managements and workers failed to agree on bonus rates, sometimes leaving thousands without wages until the Labour Department brokered a reopening. Tea garden wages and land are also central issues in north Bengal politics: on Tuesday, police arrested eleven residents of the Torsa Tea Garden in Alipurduar district at the site of a planned land port near Jaigaon, after a sit-in of more than 100 days.
